title: Learning Task Mixtures from Task Affinities: A Probabilistic Graphical Model for Supervised Fine-Tuning
abstract: arXiv:2507.12612v5 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Supervised fine-tuning performance for large language models depends strongly on how training budget is distributed across a heterogeneous set of tasks. In practice, mixtures are often fixed using simple heuristics (e.g., uniform or size-proportional sampling) that ignore task interactions, which can hurt transfer and waste budget on redundant sources. We introduce TaskPGM, a framework for learning continuous task mixtures via an energy-based model over tasks. Tasks form the nodes of a Markov random field: unary potentials capture per-task utility, and pairwise potentials encode inter-task relationships using behavioral divergences computed from predictive distributions of single-task fine-tuned models (e.g., Jensen--Shannon divergence and pointwise mutual information). Optimizing this objective yields mixtures that balance coverage against redundancy. We show that the resulting set function is weakly submodular under budget co

translated_title: 从任务亲和性学习任务混合：一种用于监督微调的概率图模型
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型的监督微调性能在很大程度上取决于训练预算如何分配到异构的任务集合上。在实践中，任务混合比例通常采用简单的启发式方法（如均匀采样或按数据规模成比例采样）来固定，这些方法忽略了任务之间的相互作用，可能会损害迁移效果，并将预算浪费在冗余的数据源上。我们提出了TaskPGM，一个通过基于能量的模型学习连续任务混合比例的框架。任务构成马尔可夫随机场中的节点：一元势能刻画每个任务的个体效用，成对势能则利用从单任务微调模型的预测分布计算出的行为差异（如Jensen–Shannon散度和逐点互信息）来编码任务间的关系。对该目标进行优化所得到的任务混合比例能够在覆盖度与冗余度之间取得平衡。我们证明了所得的集合函数在预算约束下是弱次模的……
tldr: 提出TaskPGM框架，将任务建模为马尔可夫随机场，利用单任务微调模型间的行为差异刻画任务亲和性，自动学习最优的连续任务混合比例，在监督微调中平衡覆盖度与冗余度，从而更高效地分配训练预算。
en_tdlr: TaskPGM, an energy-based probabilistic graphical model that learns optimal continuous task mixtures for supervised fine-tuning by encoding task affinities from behavioral divergences, balancing coverage against redundancy to allocate training budgets more effectively.
